proposals.mechanism: no_closure_at_lips (lips close to 3.00 cm2 at least, seal needs <0.05) and f2_floor_too_high for the rounded back vowels ao/uh/uw (F2 floor 1067-1147 Hz in their F1 bands vs targets 840/1020/870)
proposals.principle: A stop needs an articulator that seals the bore at its place. jaw_lips has a cast rest gap of 2.5-3.5 cm2, so no rest_area value seals. The lip opening is a velocity maximum of every formant, so closing and protruding the lips lowers F1, F2 and F3 together. That is the missing direction for /ɔ ʊ u/, whose best postures are already at tongue_height 0.95 at the back of the rail and still sit 11-39% high on both F1 and F2.
proposals.hypothesis: round_lips gives 0-6.6 cm2 of opening, so a full seal is possible for /p/ with the tongue lowered (airway about 1 cm2 elsewhere). With max_protrusion 1.6 cm the lip tube can grow to 2.6 cm, which lengthens the front cavity and narrows the outlet. That should pull F2 from about 1070-1140 down toward 840-1020 and bring /u/ F1 down from 418 to about 300. No params move can do this: the closure floor is fixed by the cast lip shape.
risks: aa: the largest opening falls from 6.9 to 6.6 cm2. /ɑ/ needs F1 730 (657-803), and the body reached 854, so a 0.3 cm2 loss of mouth area should cost only a few Hz of F1. Protrusion is servo-set and can stay at 0.
ae: needs F1 660 with F2 1720, which sits near the top of the 550-650 band (F2 up to 1823). The same small loss of opening applies, and protrusion stays at 0 for spread vowels.
iy/ih/eh: these need fairly open, unprotruded lips. The ring opens past the rest gap, so this should hold.
proposals.result: not kept (another proposal gained more): gained ao, p, uh, uw, lost none; costs $4.00, 57 machine min

proposals.mechanism: no_closure_at_alveolar: no articulator reaches 0-1.5 cm behind the teeth, because the rail starts at 3.25 cm and rail_start bottoms out at 2.5. Also no_closure_at_velar: the body reaches 5.5-8.5 cm but bottoms out at 0.20 cm2, because stroke 0.95 is less than the 1.2 cm bore radius.
proposals.principle: An articulator acts only within its travel and stroke. Closing the alveolar place needs a part that travels to 0.3 cm behind the teeth and seals the full bore. A body pad seals only when its cam lift is more than 1.2 cm. F3 also has velocity maxima near 1/5 and 3/5 of the tract, so two simultaneous constrictions (tip about 5 cm behind the teeth, body about 10 cm back) plus lip rounding are the only way to pull F3 toward 1690 Hz.
proposals.hypothesis: tip_tongue's blade slides 0.3-5 cm behind the teeth and can seal, which gives /t/. Setting the body stroke to 1.3 (above 1.2) lets the pad shut the velar region, which gives /k/. No value of rail_start (minimum 2.5 cm) reaches the alveolar place, so a params move cannot fix /t/. The second constriction may also start moving /ɝ/ F3 down from its 2770 Hz floor.
risks: Every held vowel: the body pad keeps the same rail and rail_start, so the old postures (height ≤0.95) remain reachable. The tip blade can retract out of the bore for vowels. A wider stroke range may make high-tongue postures slightly more noise-sensitive, but iy/ih were found at heights inside the old 0-0.95 range.
Resources: 4 servos; with round_lips the total is 6 of 6 channels. Buy 2 servos ($16) and 2 pushrod kits ($8), $24 in all, 3 days lead, 133 machine min, all within budget.

iterations.notes: I left out long_cast. Scaling to a 17-17.5 cm tract would require the original body to hit F1 of about 700-850 Hz together with F2 of about 1800-2200 Hz to keep /æ/, but its 650-900 Hz F1 band reaches F2 of only 1662 Hz, so /æ/ would break. /ɝ/ (F3 1690 vs a 2770 Hz floor) most likely needs round_lips and tip_tongue together, with constrictions at the lips, about 5 cm and about 10 cm behind the teeth. Combining those two swaps uses all 6 channels and costs $24 with 3 days lead.
